business_model.claim: Tutor Perini sells general contracting, construction management and design-build services to private customers and public agencies.
quotes: is a leading construction company offering diversified general contracting, construction management and design-build services to private customers and public agencies throughout the world.

business_model.claim: The company self-performs many trades on its projects and worked on approximately 1,600 construction projects during 2025.
quotes: During 2025, we performed work on approximately 1,600 construction projects.

business_model.claim: The business reports three segments: Civil, Building and Specialty Contractors.
quotes: Our business is conducted through three segments: Civil, Building and Specialty Contractors.

business_model.basis: stated in P1; figures from the P6 segment table
business_model.claim: Civil builds public works and infrastructure such as highways, bridges, tunnels and mass transit, and it was the largest segment in the first nine months of 2026, with revenue from external customers of $2,407,385 and income from construction operations of $337,493 (table in thousands).
quotes: Our Civil segment specializes in public works construction and the replacement and reconstruction of infrastructure across several major geographic regions of the United States.

business_model.claim: Civil customers award contracts either by competitive bid, where price is the main factor, or by best-value proposal.
quotes: the traditional public “competitive bid” method, in which price is the major determining factor

business_model.basis: stated in P1; figures from P6
business_model.claim: Building serves private and public customers in specialized markets including hospitality and gaming, healthcare, education and government facilities; its nine-month 2026 revenue from external customers was $1,573,110 and its income from construction operations was $74,781 (table in thousands).
quotes: Our Building segment has significant experience providing services to several specialized building markets for private and public works customers, including hospitality and gaming, transportation, healthcare, commercial offices, government facilities, sports and entertainment, education, correctional and detention facilities, biotech, pharmaceutical, industrial and technology.

business_model.basis: stated in P1; figures from P6
business_model.claim: Specialty Contractors performs electrical, mechanical, plumbing, HVAC and fire protection work, much of it for the Civil and Building segments; its nine-month 2026 revenue from external customers was $766,266 and its income from construction operations was $16,398 (table in thousands).
quotes: A significant portion of the segment's work has been, and is expected to continue to be, performed for our Civil and Building segments, although the segment also continues to contract directly with state and local municipal agencies, real estate developers, school districts and other commercial and industrial customers.

business_model.claim: Government entities accounted for 86% of backlog as of December 31, 2025, which makes public spending the main demand source.
quotes: The percentage of our business coming from government entities has continued to increase in recent years, and as of December 31, 2025 accounted for 86% of our backlog.

business_model.claim: Public funding sources drive Civil demand; the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law provided $1.2 trillion, but its current funding window closes on September 30, 2026.
quotes: While the current funding window for the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law closes on September 30, 2026

business_model.claim: International work, including U.S. territories, provided $489.7 million, or 9%, of 2025 revenue.
quotes: For the year ended December 31, 2025, we derived $489.7 million, or 9%, of revenue from our work on projects in international locations, including U.S. territories.

business_model.claim: Operations are concentrated in New York and California.
quotes: Lastly, we are more susceptible to adverse economic conditions in New York and California, as a significant portion of our operations are concentrated in those states.

business_model.claim: Revenue comes from converting awarded backlog into work performed; Civil backlog typically converts over three to five years, and Building and Specialty Contractors backlog over one to three years.
quotes: Backlog in our industry is a measure of the total value of work that is remaining to be performed on projects that have been awarded.

Most projects in the Civil segment’s backlog typically convert to revenue over a period of three to five years and in the Building and Specialty Contractors segments over a period of one to three years.

business_model.claim: Backlog was $20.4 billion at September 30, 2026, down 6% from $21.6 billion a year earlier.
quotes: Consolidated backlog as of September 30, 2026 was $20.4 billion, up compared to $19.9 billion at the end of the second quarter of 2026, and down 6% compared to $21.6 billion at the end of the third quarter of 2025.

business_model.claim: New awards, which replenish backlog, were $4.5 billion in the first nine months of 2026 against $7.0 billion a year earlier.
quotes: Consolidated new awards for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 totaled $2.2 billion and $4.5 billion, respectively, compared to $2.0 billion and $7.0 billion for the same periods in 2025.

business_model.basis: stated in P4; figures from P6
business_model.claim: Recent revenue growth has come from increased execution on newer, larger and higher-margin projects; nine-month 2026 revenue was $4,746,761 against $4,035,674 a year earlier (table in thousands).
quotes: primarily driven by increased project execution activities on certain newer, larger and higher-margin projects that have significant scope of work remaining.

business_model.claim: Design-build projects generate smaller revenue and earnings during an initial design phase and larger amounts during the later construction phase.
quotes: Many of the Company’s newer projects are design-build projects that have an initial six to eighteen month design phase during which smaller revenue and earnings are generated prior to the start of a multi-year construction phase that generates substantially larger revenue and earnings.

business_model.claim: Cost of operations is the dominant cost: in the first nine months of 2026 it was (4,159,388), leaving gross profit of 587,373 (table in thousands).

business_model.claim: To limit cost escalation, the company buys out materials early and uses fixed-price subcontracts that pass escalation risk to subcontractors.
quotes: Also at that time, the Company enters into fixed-price contracts with its key project subcontractors whereby the risk of unforeseen escalation is transferred to the subcontractors.

business_model.claim: Profit depends on estimates at completion; changes in estimates, claims, litigation and settlements move reported earnings, and in 2025 legal judgments or decisions had net unfavorable impacts of $32.5 million.
quotes: If we are unable to accurately estimate contract risks, revenue or costs, we may incur a loss or achieve lower than anticipated profit.

Both periods of 2026 were also positively impacted by a significant decrease in share-based compensation expense of $39.5 million and $43.5 million, respectively, compared to the same periods in 2025.

growth_thesis.claim: Sustaining backlog requires new awards to keep pace with revenue burn. Q3 2026 was a second straight quarter of book-to-burn above 1.0x, but nine-month awards were $4.5 billion against $7.0 billion a year earlier.

Consolidated new awards for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 totaled $2.2 billion and $4.5 billion, respectively, compared to $2.0 billion and $7.0 billion for the same periods in 2025.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated by management in P6 and P4.
growth_thesis.claim: The future award source is a pipeline of more than $200 billion over the next three to four years. Converting it requires winning bids, many of which are expected in 2027.
quotes: Overall, the Company's pipeline of potential projects over the next three to four years totals more than $200 billion, which is approximately three times larger than the pipeline from just a couple of years ago.

The Company expects a significant number of large opportunities to bid in 2027, all of which are well aligned with the Company's disciplined bidding strategy and preferred contractual and margin characteristics.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P4; the counter-risk is stated in P2.
growth_thesis.claim: Management attributes its award success partly to limited competition on some larger projects. That condition must persist for wins and margins to hold.
quotes: favorable market dynamics, including limited competition in select markets for some of the larger projects

In addition, evolving changes in the construction industry, such as the trend toward an increased use of the progressive design-build project delivery method that may reduce project risks for both owners and contractors, could result in increased competition and potentially lower margins on certain projects in the future.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated as management expectation in P3; P6 reiterates.
growth_thesis.claim: Building segment projects in preconstruction are a further driver, including a multi-billion-dollar California healthcare project. This depends on those projects moving into construction.
quotes: These projects are expected to transition from preconstruction to construction over the next few years, and they include a large, multi-billion-dollar healthcare project in California that is anticipated to be incrementally added to backlog over the next two to three years.

growth_thesis.claim: Growth depends on public funding: government entities accounted for 86% of backlog. The current Bipartisan Infrastructure Law funding window closes on September 30, 2026, and the amount of future funding is undetermined.
quotes: The percentage of our business coming from government entities has continued to increase in recent years, and as of December 31, 2025 accounted for 86% of our backlog.

While the current funding window for the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law closes on September 30, 2026, we believe that Congress recognizes the long-term nature of infrastructure work and is already engaged in the legislative process to secure future funding beyond that date, although any amount and composition of such future funding is yet to be determined.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated as a risk in P2.
growth_thesis.claim: Executing backlog requires enough skilled labour and subcontractors. Rapid backlog growth has constrained labour before.
quotes: A significant, rapid growth in our backlog has led, and could continue to lead, to situations in which labor resources become constrained.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated as a risk in P2.
growth_thesis.claim: Winning new contracts requires continued access to reasonably priced surety bonds.
quotes: If we are unable to obtain reasonably priced surety bonds in the future, it could significantly affect our ability to be awarded new contracts and could, consequently, have a material adverse effect on our business, results of operations and financial condition.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P4; amounts in F3.
growth_thesis.claim: Earnings growth was helped by lower share-based compensation expense, down $39.5 million in Q3 and $43.5 million over nine months. The nine-month expense fell to 77,179 from 120,676 (table in thousands).
quotes: Both periods of 2026 were also positively impacted by a significant decrease in share-based compensation expense of $39.5 million and $43.5 million, respectively, compared to the same periods in 2025.

growth_thesis.claim: For the compensation benefit to persist, the company must not reissue liability-classified awards. It stopped issuing them after shareholders approved additional plan shares.
quotes: After the Company’s shareholders approved additional shares under the Plan in May 2025, the Company stopped issuing liability-classified, long-term incentive compensation awards, which will help to reduce future earnings volatility.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P4; figures in F2.
growth_thesis.claim: The July 2026 refinancing is expected to cut interest expense. Q3 interest expense was (7,290) against (13,549) a year earlier (table in thousands), and the refinancing cost a $51.4 million loss on extinguishment.
quotes: extended debt maturities, is expected to significantly reduce future interest expense, more than doubled the size of its available revolving credit facility and provided meaningfully improved terms

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P6; the counter is inferred from the F1 balance sheet.
growth_thesis.claim: Operating cash flow grew with volume: $330.9 million in Q3 and $665.1 million over nine months, up 14% and 16%. Billings in excess of costs rose to 2,044,207 from 1,838,610 (table in thousands).
quotes: The record operating cash flow for both periods was driven by higher volume, strong execution, record earnings and collections on profitable projects.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated as management expectation in P6.
growth_thesis.claim: Management raised 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $5.90 to $6.10, from $5.15 to $5.45. It expects strong revenue and adjusted EPS growth in 2027 based on backlog visibility.
quotes: The Company also anticipates continued strong revenue and adjusted EPS growth in 2027 due to solid visibility provided by its high-quality, long-duration backlog.

material_events.basis: stated in the cited item (P4), with the charge shown as a line in F2
material_events.claim: The company completed a refinancing of its senior notes and an amendment and restatement of its revolving credit facility, recognizing a one-time loss on extinguishment of debt of $51.4 million, which included a $35.6 million cash redemption premium.
quotes: As a result of this transaction, the Company recognized a one-time loss on extinguishment of debt of $51.4 million ($0.70 per diluted share, after tax) for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, which consisted of a $35.6 million cash redemption premium and $15.8 million of non-cash expense related to the acceleration of previously unamortized discounts and deferred financing costs.

material_events.claim: The company settled its obligations under its defined benefit pension plan and recorded a one-time non-cash charge of $33.8 million.
quotes: In the third quarter of 2026, the Company settled its obligations under its defined benefit pension plan to eliminate future cash contributions and associated ongoing administrative expenses.

This resulted in a one-time non-cash charge of $33.8 million ($0.40 per diluted share, after tax) primarily related to the accelerated recognition of unamortized net actuarial losses, which would otherwise have been recognized in future periods.

material_events.claim: In its earnings release, the company raised its full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $5.90 to $6.10, up from $5.15 to $5.45.
quotes: Raising 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $5.90 to $6.10 (up from $5.15 to $5.45)
